title: SREV-327 Secure AppInfo binding handle layout probe
stage: data -> schema -> topology -> logic -> action -> verify
contracts: official RPC binding handles are opaque RPC runtime objects, not structures Sandboxie may parse by contract
RpcBindingInqObject is the supported first route for reading an object UUID from a binding handle
RPC_ASYNC_STATE owns only the documented async state and notification shape
Secure_CheckElevation uses RpcBindingInqObject first and the local observed AppInfo binding layout probe only as a compatibility fallback
fallback layout probe must keep the small-handle guard before any fixed-offset GUID read
OFFSET_OF_BINDING_GUID values are local evidence, not official Microsoft binding-handle ABI

runtime proof must classify BindingHandle and record whether the official object UUID query or fallback layout probe matched before changing offsets, guards, GUID comparison, or __try exception behavior
SREV-327 adds an official object UUID query path while preserving fallback UAC elevation detection behavior
SREV-326 and SREV-327 share docs/plan/srev-326-327-secure-runtime-capture.schema.json as the machine-readable Windows evidence shape

binding_value_classes: official RPC handle-like value if observed
probe_outputs: official object UUID match or miss
negative_controls: binding value below the small-handle guard
unreadable page at the binding pointer

runtime_gate: Capture AppInfo UAC elevation calls on supported Windows 10/11 builds and x64/WOW64 where supported, then prove BindingHandle value class, async-state fields, guard result, GUID probe result, __try exception path, elevation type, result handle slot, process image, AppInfo call identity, and negative controls before any behavior change
